newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon denounces killings of Israeli schoolgirls.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon denounces killings of Israeli schoolgirls.

text.p: Lebanon denounced on Friday the killing of seven Israeli schoolgirls on the Israeli-Jordanian border but questioned whether the world community had denounced Israel's killing of civilians in south Lebanon in 1996.
"I denounce what happened to the students but I want to ask whether the world denounced the killing of the children and women in Qana," President Elias Hrawi told a medical conference.
He was referring to the killing of more than 100 Lebanese civilians in Israel's April 18, 1996 shelling of the headquarters of a Fijian U.N. battalion in the south Lebanon village of Qana.

"There were tears in Jordan by some who cut short a visit to Europe to return home and condemn the incident. Did they denounce what happened to us in Qana?" Hrawi added, apparently referring to Jordan's King Hussein, who broke off a visit to Spain after Thursday's shootings by a lone Jordanian soldier.
Hrawi was speaking as Lebanon marked the 19th anniversary of Israel's first invasion of the country.
Lebanon and Israel are officially in a state of war. Peace efforts have been stalled over the issue of Israeli withdrawal from a 15-km (nine-mile) wide south Lebanon occupation zone.
